title: BIS Quarterly Review, December 2025
summary: The BIS Quarterly Review December 2025 covers international banking and financial market developments, with substantial focus on market structure topics including FX derivatives turnover trends from the 2025 Triennial Survey, the cash-futures basis trade dynamics, and the ongoing LIBOR benchmark reform transition in interest rate derivatives markets. The publication examines structural shifts in global FX and IRD markets amid monetary policy changes and identifies clearing concentration as an emerging challenge for EMEs.
key_points: 2025 BIS Triennial Survey reveals surge in FX volumes, with hedging activity playing a centre stage role in market dynamics
Cash-futures basis trade is identified as a key structural feature affecting interest rate derivatives trading on exchanges
Global interest rate derivatives markets are undergoing structural shifts driven by LIBOR benchmark reform and monetary policy expectations
EMEs face remaining challenges in OTC IRD markets including clearing concentration issues
Renminbi is driving growth in EME currency trading volumes
Geographical shifts show migration of euro contracts to Germany as part of post-LIBOR transition
why_it_matters: This BIS publication provides authoritative, source-grounded data on fundamental market structure elements: FX market liquidity conditions, basis trade dynamics, and clearing infrastructure. For traders and risk managers, understanding the cash-futures basis relationship and clearing concentration patterns is essential for assessing funding risks and execution quality in IRD and FX markets.
macro_context: The research notes shifts in FX trading amid global monetary policy tightening cycles and links volatility challenges to risk-taking behavior. Sovereign yields moderated with monetary easing, while precious metals and USD appreciated.
market_structure_context: Core market structure content includes: (1) FX market liquidity conditions and non-visible trading patterns, (2) cash-futures basis trade dynamics and XTD positioning, (3) clearing concentration challenges in EME OTC IRD markets, (4) migration of LIBOR-referenced contracts to new benchmarks, (5) broker-dealer and electronic broker landscape in FX execution.
